lessons.name: Use spelling patterns to sort long and short vowel words

contents.text: <instructions>Sort the words by their vowel sounds.</instructions>
Vowels can be short or long. A long vowel says its name. A short vowel does not.

header.text: When a vowel is followed by just consonants, it usually does not say its name. It makes a short vowel sound instead.
When a vowel is followed by a consonant and a silent e, the vowel says its name. It makes a long vowel sound.

When a vowel is followed by another vowel, the two vowels sometimes make a vowel team. The first vowel in a vowel team says its name. It makes a long vowel sound. The other vowel is silent. Some vowel teams are ai, ee, ea, ie, oa, and ue.

"Hooray! It is time to eat," cheer Finn and Lee.

They sit and have a little meal. They fill their cups with a drop of tea. "Mm, this tea is very sweet!" says Snail.
They each have one green pea and a bit of cheese. "Can I have more treats, please?" asks Snail.
Flea gives his friend a bite of pie.
"This feels like a feast!" says Snail.
"I think so, too!" smiles Flea.

alternativeText.text: A man sits in his boat on the water. A fish is jumping out of the water and smiling at the boy.

textContent.text: It is a sunny day. Dean takes his boat out to sea.
He sees some fish swim in the weeds. He hears them speak. "These are magic fish!" says Dean.
Dean wants to feed the fish. He thinks they need a treat. "Do you eat cheese?" Dean asks the fish.
One fish leaps out of the water. "Just swim with us, please!" the fish tells Dean.
"Hey, that would be really neat!" Dean cheers.
He jumps deep into the sea.

content.text: Where does Dean see the fish?
